name: Brunner-Winkle Bird
summary: Late-1920s New York three-seat sport and joyriding biplane known for easy handling; a rare antique today.

wings: Staggered single-bay biplane with external struts and wire bracing
Upper wing is much larger than the lower wing (about twice the area)
engines: Kinner K-5 radial, usually uncowled with exposed cylinders (early model had a water-cooled OX-5 V-8)
fuselage: Open cockpits seating three, with the pilot behind two passengers
Forward fuselage skinned in metal, aft fabric-covered

tellTales: Biplane whose upper wing is much larger than the lower wing
Rare three-seat open-cockpit 1920s biplane with an exposed radial
Metal-skinned forward fuselage on a biplane

confusedWith.howToTell: The Waco 10 has wings of similar size and an all-fabric fuselage; the Bird has an upper wing about twice the area of the lower and a metal-skinned forward fuselage.
The Travel Air has big overhanging balanced ailerons; the Bird has conventional ailerons.
The Fleet is a two-seater with tandem cockpits; the Bird seats three.
